question: The release of which hormone causes simultaneous increase in heartbeat and breathing rate?
solution:
The correct answer is **Adrenaline**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adrenaline**, also known as epinephrine, is a hormone and medication.
 
• It is produced by both the adrenal glands and certain neurons.
 
• It plays an important role in the fight-or-flight response by increasing blood flow to muscles, output of the heart, pupil dilation, and blood sugar level.
 
• It does so by binding to alpha and beta receptors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adrenaline** was first isolated and identified in 1895 by Napoleon Cybulski, a Polish physiologist.
 
• It is used medically to treat a number of conditions, including anaphylaxis, cardiac arrest, and superficial bleeding.
 
• In the brain, adrenaline affects areas involved in attention and responding actions, enhancing memory consolidation.
 
• Commercially, synthetic adrenaline is produced through a process of chemical synthesis.
